sentence: This project builds engineered dendritic cells that target and eliminate tumors as if they were an infection.
This project tests whether a test of olfaction and machine learning can classify the stage of Alzheimer's disease.
This project provides microscopy and image analysis services for cancer research, including imaging of cells and molecules.
This project builds a high-throughput assay to find inhibitors of efflux pumps, which help bacteria evade antibiotics.
This project supports data and biospecimen collection for studies of inherited susceptibility to cancer in African Americans.
This project supports the sequencing and analysis of multi-omics data and builds a web portal to share that data.
This project tries to make exosomes positively charged so they can enter cartilage and deliver gene therapeutics to repair cartilage and provide pain relief.
This project provides laboratory services in virology, immunology, proteomics and bioinformatics to HIV investigators.
This project studies how signaling in endothelial cells controls blood vessel integrity and development in zebrafish and human cells.
This project builds an imaging agent to map myeloperoxidase activity in the brain and tests it in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how the three-dimensional folding of the genome links to gene expression, focusing on cohesin complexes and DNA loops.
This project provides support in research design, biostatistics and bioinformatics for research on chronic diseases.
This project studies how the metabolite itaconate is produced in brain tumors and how it affects tumor growth and response to therapy.
This project studies whether a peptide from the same family as opioid peptides may cause cognitive impairment in people with Alcohol Use Disorder.
This project tests whether a protein that binds fatty acids affects inflammation, metabolism and disease progression in models of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project builds an AI framework to find protein-protein interactions that suppress an immune pathway in Kaposi Sarcoma.
This project tests whether chest radiography can identify people in subclinical stages of disease so that steps can be taken to interrupt transmission.
This project uses bioinformatic methods to study why some carriers of Clostridioides difficile go on to develop disease and others do not.
This project studies how the primary cilium, a sensory organelle, is altered in neurons of patients with tuberous sclerosis complex.
This project builds microfluidic organ-on-a-chip models to study how osteoblasts and bone endothelial cells affect breast cancer metastasis to bone.
